subject: Performance SLO follow-up: concurrency, streaming, and context limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co...@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@fintechco.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up: concurrency, streaming, and context limits

Hi Ethan + Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps we agreed on. I focused this on the performance items where you wanted concrete numbers and trade-offs so your infra team can sketch capacity models.

Recap (short):
- Primary SLO target: p95 response latency ≤ 300ms for interactive sessions (chat assistant).
- Target concurrency: start at 50 concurrent live users, with headroom to 150 at peak.
- Streaming: required for user-perceived latency on long responses (partial token streaming / SSE).
- Context window expectation: average input ~1.2k tokens, heavy tail up to 6k tokens; desired output up to 2k tokens for long-form summaries.

Key trade-offs we highlighted:
- Larger input (4k-8k) increases per-request compute and can push p95 well beyond 300ms on single-GPU instances unless using efficient kernel paths or sharded inference.
- Buffered batching improves throughput but increases tail latency; for interactive chat we recommended small max batch sizes (4-8) and elastic batching for background jobs.
- Streaming preserves perceived latency even if full completion is slower — important for user experience with 1k+ token outputs.

Attachments I shared after the call (attached to this thread):
- MAA_draft_FintechCo_v1.pdf (mutual action plan / timeline)
- slo-summary-quickview.csv (simple capacity math and examples)
- sample-usage-payloads.jsonl (anonymized prompt length distribution)

Next steps (agreed):
1) Tech deep-dive: schedule 60m session with your infra + our runtime engineer (Stephanie) to walk through payloads and SLO tuning.
2) You to share 3 days of representative prompt logs or the distribution (we used sample-usage-payloads.jsonl as template).
3) We (Redwood) will run a short capacity/latency simulation and return a recommended deployment pattern (dedicated pool sizing, quantization suggestion, and streaming config) within 4 business days after we receive logs.
4) Legal/Proc: I'll drop a first-pass MAA (attached) and Ben will follow up on pricing scenarios tied to reserved capacity once we validate throughput.

Please reply with preferred times for the deep-dive (we have availability Mon/Tue next week 10-2 PT), and confirm you can share the sample logs by end of week.

Best,
Marissa

From: Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@fintechco.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: concurrency, streaming, and context limits

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so the deep-dive can be focused:

1) Our measurable SLOs: we need p95 ≤ 300ms for the interactive flows (customer-facing chat). For background batch jobs (e.g., nightly summarization) we can tolerate higher latency but want cost-efficient throughput.

2) Context window: our current client usage shows inputs typically 800-1,500 tokens; occasional analyst queries are up to 6k tokens. We are evaluating increasing to 8k in Q3 but that will be a separate ask.

3) Output size: in normal chat the outputs are 150-400 tokens; in summary mode we expect 1k-2k tokens. Streaming on the chat path is mandatory.

4) Concurrency: baseline 50 concurrent chat sessions, with spikes to ~120 during peak trading hours (06:00-10:00 PT). We need predictable tail behavior during spikes.

Question for Redwood:
- Given the constraints above, what is the recommended model variant / quantization profile to keep p95 ≤ 300ms for up to 2k outputs when inputs are ~1-1.5k? Also, what's the expected p99 hit when you enable streaming (i.e., does streaming meaningfully change p99 for full completion times)?

We can provide 72h of anonymized prompt logs by end of day tomorrow. Schedule wise, Tue 16 Mar 10:00 PT works for our infra folks.

Thanks,
Ethan
CTO, FintechCo
ethan.shaw@fintechco.com

Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: concurrency, streaming, and context limits

Ethan — great, and thanks for the clarifications. Quick answers and what we'll bring to Tue's deep-dive: 

Short answers now: 
- Recommended starting config (interactive): a dedicted pool running an 8-bit quantized 13B-class open model variant with optimized kernels; target per-GPU concurrent requests tuned to keep batching small (2-8) and p95 ≤ 300ms for inputs around 1-1.5k and outputs up to ~1k.
- For your 1k-2k output scenario we expect p95 to push toward ~350-450ms on single-card setups unless we increase replication or use a 2-card sharded setup; we'll show concrete numbers in the capacity sim.
- Streaming: streaming does not lower the total compute required for full completion, but it improves time-to-first-token dramatically (often <100ms) and improves perceived latency for users; it does not materially reduce p99 full completion time unless combined with higher parallelism.

What we'll bring to the deep-dive (deliverables):
- Stephanie will walk through a short simulation using your prompt distribution and three config options: single-card quantized, dual-card sharded, and small dedicated pool with autoscale.
- A short CSV with expected p50/p95/p99 for each config and for baseline prompt percentiles (50th, 90th, 99th).
- A cost estimate delta between the three configs and notes on when to move to reserved capacity vs. burst.

Prep for the session: please upload the anonymized prompt logs to the Drive link I shared (or send sample files directly) and confirm Tue 16 Mar 10:00 PT.

I'll also flag Ben to start the pricing scenarios based on whichever config looks best in the simulation.

Best —
Marissa
